name: Royal Free Hospital
opening_hours: If the patient needs to be seen as an emergency: the emergency eye doctor should be bleeped – GPs/ optoms should call 020 7794 0500 extension 33625 or bleep 1758.
opening_hours_full:
If the patient needs to be seen as an emergency: the emergency eye doctor should be bleeped – GPs/ optoms should call 020 7794 0500 extension 33625 or bleep 1758.
 
After this a referral document can be emailed to rf.eyecasualty@nhs.net
 
If there is no answer to the bleep/ phone then email the above address and in the subject line write Call back urgently for advice please (and leave a reliable number).
 
If a patient with a clinical concern makes contact with yourselves and is known to us, then they need to attend our general casualty for review and then they will discuss with the clinic about accepting the patient in hours or call the on call doctor when out of hours.
 
If attend anywhere has assessed/ triaged the patient already and then needs to be physically seen by us as they are local to us, then please either contact the clinician on call in casualty on 020 7794 0500 extension 33625 or bleep 1758 if it is an emergency, or email through to us the letter from the consultation with the patient's details and we can call them to arrange an appointment if not urgent.

How to refer:
Please note that walk-ins/self-referrals are NOT accepted. 
 
Please complete the referral form below and email it to moorfields.sghurgentcare@nhs.net 
 
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-elgkdhc4HZhoZgRA0iTwOlYIAN8vO0Z/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=104561831344168348650&rtpof=true&sd=true

(Click File > Download > Microsoft Word)
 
The referrals will be triaged within 4 hours during working hours, and the patient will be contacted directly to arrange a review if needed (please do not ask the patient to just turn up). 
 
If your referral is urgent, please call the triage line and send an e-referral form as above. 

08:30-21:00 Mon-Sun - 02077025542
21:00 - 08:30 Night nurse triage - 07921056594


If a patient is seen at Kingston, St Heliers, Epsom or Croydon Hospitals out of hours, refer to St George's via telephone and email if ocular emergency. Refer via local pathways for other cases.

CUES
For patients with non-urgent sight or life-threatening conditions (e.g. red eye or eyelids, flashes and floaters (more than 72 hours*), dry, gritty and uncomfortable eyes, sticky discharge or watery eye, foreign body sensation in the eye) who are registered with a GP in Merton/Wandsworth, Richmond and Kingston, please refer to one of the participating high street opticians https://www.primaryeyecare.co.uk/find-a-practice/
